owner.name: Konrad Waleszczyński
owner.headline: Renewable energy data analytics
owner.intro: Analytics for solar, wind and battery assets: performance verification, fault detection, power market analysis and dashboards. Every project below is written from scratch on open data or on a disclosed synthetic plant and can be rerun from its repository, with tests and CI.

data_sources: Kelmarsh wind farm SCADA (Cubico, CC BY 4.0)

projects.title: Polish power market, live
projects.summary: Self-updating dashboard of the Polish electricity market built from PSE open data every afternoon: prices, spreads, negative prices, generation mix and battery potential.
projects.highlight: No server and no database: GitHub Actions rebuilds a static page from cached monthly Parquet files.

projects.title: How solar eats its own price in Poland
projects.summary: Capture prices and value factors of PV and wind from 15-minute PSE data since June 2024, negative prices, the Polish duck curve and a PV build-out scenario with a hindcast.
projects.highlight: In 2025 PV captured 64 % of the average price and wind 94 %; every 10 pp of PV share costs PV about 0.20 of value factor.

projects.title: Battery arbitrage on Polish prices
projects.summary: Mixed-integer dispatch of a battery on 15-minute RCE prices, solved for every delivery day, with sensitivity to duration, efficiency and cycle limits.
projects.highlight: 859-day backtest: a 2-hour battery earned 308 k PLN per MW in 2025, and negative prices reached 354 hours that year.

projects.title: Battery revenue stacking in Poland
projects.summary: Day-ahead arbitrage co-optimised with balancing capacity (FCR, aFRR, mFRR, RR) on PSE data since June 2024, a capacity market layer, and how much battery capacity the shallow reserve markets can absorb, from the published offer stacks.
projects.highlight: Over the last 12 months a 2-hour battery could stack about 3.3 m PLN/MW against 0.38 m from arbitrage alone, but a fleet of 1 GW cuts that by about 70 %.

projects.title: Battery paper trading, live track record
projects.summary: Every morning before the day-ahead gate closure a forecast of tomorrow's prices and an optimal 1 MW / 2 MWh battery plan; the next day it is settled on real prices and appended to a ledger that is never recomputed.
projects.highlight: Backtest since June 2024: forecast + MILP earns 83 % of perfect foresight (324 k PLN/MW/yr), but a plain 7-day price average does as well; live record from 28 Oct 2026.

projects.title: When batteries flatten their own spreads
projects.summary: A 0-10 GW battery fleet dispatched against an empirical Polish supply curve from PSE data: how spreads, revenue per MW, negative-price hours and the evening peak change as storage grows.
projects.highlight: At 2025 prices a 2-hour battery earns 308 k PLN/MW alone, 203 k at 2 GW of fleet and 72 k at 10 GW; the marginal value of the fleet turns negative near 10 GW.

projects.title: Cable pooling: PV, wind and storage behind one connection
projects.summary: How much PV, wind and battery storage to build behind a shared grid connection in Poland: ERA5 profiles, RCE prices and an hourly LP dispatch for 856 size combinations per site, with NPV, LCOE and curtailment.
projects.highlight: Best oversizing is 1.75-2.25x the connection without a battery and 2.75-3x with one, curtailing 9-20 % of the energy.

projects.title: How real batteries trade
projects.summary: One year of 5-minute AEMO data for the 40 batteries of 20 MW or more in Australia's NEM, compared day by day with perfect-foresight arbitrage.
projects.highlight: The six largest batteries earn 11-51 % of their perfect-foresight optimum; the gap is split into capacity offered, volume and timing.

projects.title: Battery state of charge and ageing
projects.summary: State of charge rebuilt from market data and checked against the operator's own SoC, an LFP ageing model fitted to lab cell data, and degradation-aware arbitrage.
projects.highlight: SoC from 5-minute market data tracks the operator's SoC within 2.7-3.8 percentage points (RMSE).

projects.title: Grid battery operations against warranty and LTSA
projects.summary: Monthly warranty and LTSA reporting for an operating grid battery: SoC-corrected round-trip efficiency with and without auxiliaries, time-, capacity- and energy-based availability, rainflow cycles, warranty violations, capacity tests with guard bands, and a benchmark of all 55 grid batteries in Australia's NEM validated against ACEN's New England BESS data.
projects.highlight: Across 55 NEM batteries conversion RTE is 0.92, but metered RTE is 0.82 median (0.75 for 1 h, 0.88 for 4 h) because of auxiliaries and standby drain; PASA technical availability is 95.8 % median while commercial offered availability is 78.1 %.

projects.title: Battery ageing vs capacity market obligation
projects.summary: LFP ageing under real RCE arbitrage and capped-cycling profiles against a 17-year Polish capacity market contract: when the battery falls short, and overbuild, augmentation or module replacement compared in NPV and risk.
projects.highlight: Built to nominal energy, a battery misses its obligation in year one; +20 % headroom lasts 7-10 years, and full arbitrage leaves 62-68 % SoH after 17 years.

projects.title: Home and C&I energy management on 15-minute Polish prices
projects.summary: Daily MILP vs rule-based control of rooftop PV, battery, floor-slab heat pump and EV under Polish 12-month FIFO net-billing (RCE), and of a B23 commercial site under the capacity fee (K1-K4), on real PSE prices and ERA5 weather with synthetic loads; set-points are replayed over a localhost Modbus TCP emulator with a watchdog.
projects.highlight: Over Oct 2025 - Sep 2026 the noisy-forecast MILP cuts a dynamic-tariff house's annual cost by 37.4 % (2,378 PLN/yr); on the commercial site a causal ratio rule puts 88.5 % of working days in K1, against a perfect-foresight MILP bound of 98.4 %.

projects.title: Container thermal balance, HVAC auxiliary load and net RTE of a grid battery
projects.summary: Coupled electro-thermal and auxiliary-power model of a 2.5 MW / 5 MWh LFP container in 2025 ERA5 Polish weather: Joule and entropic cell heat, liquid-cooling chiller vs forced-air DX, heater, pumps, PCS and MV transformer losses, with round-trip efficiency at every metering boundary for reserve, arbitrage and two-cycle duty.
projects.highlight: Net RTE at the PCC is 92.4 % at 1 cycle/day with 0.18 C peaks and 88.2 % at the rated 0.5 C; at 0.35 cycles/day it is 89.8 %, because fixed transformer and control loads, not winter, weigh on low cycling. Reported fleet averages are nearer 82 %, so the model is an optimistic bound.

projects.title: Corporate PPA structuring and shaping risk on Polish power prices
projects.summary: Pay-as-produced vs baseload and two-shift corporate PPAs settled on PSE RCE prices: a four-term decomposition into price level, shape, volume and residual exposure, negative-price clauses, and PV : wind mixes with no battery or a 2 h / 4 h battery across 500 bootstrap years of 2025 weeks.
projects.highlight: In 2025 a baseload PPA cost a pure PV seller 153.5 PLN/MWh of shaping cost against 27.0 for pure wind, with no interior optimum: cost and P90 are best at 100 % wind, while 24/7 hourly matching peaks at a mix (76.6 % at 80 % wind, 84.2 % with a 4 h battery).

projects.title: PV budget bridge: monthly P50 to actual waterfall and sensor QC
projects.summary: Monthly asset-management bridge from P50 budget to measured production (irradiance, temperature, degradation, soiling, snow, clipping, availability, curtailment, data gaps and unexplained residual), weather-corrected PR, contractual guarantee tests and pyranometer QC, checked on NREL PVDAQ and synthetic Polish plants.
projects.highlight: Recovers injected outages and curtailment within 0.5 % on synthetic truth and flags clock shifts, sensor tilt errors and pyranometer drift across three multi-year NREL PVDAQ rooftops.

projects.title: PV shading from AC power alone
projects.summary: Sun-path residual fingerprinting finds, draws and costs obstructions from 15-minute AC power, without an irradiance sensor, a site visit or a drone.
projects.highlight: A building's silhouette recovered with mask IoU 0.93 and 0.8 deg RMSE on simulated systems, then run on two years of a real PVDAQ roof.

projects.title: Single-axis trackers in 3D
projects.summary: Row-to-row shading projected onto module cells with a bypass-diode string model: true tracking vs backtracking vs slope-aware backtracking near Poznań.
projects.highlight: Backtracking gives +4.3 % DC yield over true tracking on flat ground (1255 vs 1204 kWh/kWp).

projects.title: PV outages: detection, cause and availability
projects.summary: Seven ways to find production losses at string, inverter and meter level (threshold, expected PR model, peer median, Hampel, CUSUM, isolation forest, gradient boosting) plus a hybrid, cause classification, lost energy and IEC 61724-1 style availability on a simulated plant with ground truth, real PVDAQ data and an open shading dataset.
projects.highlight: Requiring events of at least 1 h lifts the hybrid detector's event precision from 0.14 to 0.74 and cuts false alarms from 2.9 to 0.13 per device-year; thresholds tuned on simulation give 257 alarms per inverter-year on real roofs, a short site set-up brings it to 6 with all real outages still found.

projects.title: PV fault detection: autoencoder vs baselines
projects.summary: A PyTorch autoencoder against a PR threshold, an ASTM E2848 regression and a pvlib model, scored per fault type on 20 injected faults and on real PVDAQ data.
projects.highlight: F1 0.77 against 0.37-0.48 for the baselines; on real data it caught an inverter outage reported 10 days late by the inverter itself.

projects.title: PV thermal check: modules, inverter, transformer
projects.summary: Module temperature models (Faiman, SAPM, PVsyst, Ross) fitted on PVDAQ data with cell temperature recovered from open-circuit voltage, temperature-corrected PR, sensor-fault detection, inverter and transformer thermal checks, and losses moved to Poland.
projects.highlight: The back-of-module sensor saw only about half of the real heating: thermal losses are 10.5 % a year, not 6.7 %; temperature-corrected PR cuts the seasonal spread from 13.1 to 4.8 pp.

projects.title: PV string fault diagnosis from inverter MPPT voltage and current
projects.summary: Separating shorted bypass diodes, PID, extra series resistance, obstacle shading and soiling from 15-minute inverter MPPT voltage and current alone. A sub-string one-diode model generates synthetic telemetry with faults of known size; a separate estimator is tuned on one set of inverters and scored on another.
projects.highlight: Held-out macro-F1 is 0.694 with 7 % false alarms on healthy windows: shorted diodes are counted exactly in 97.9 % of detected cases and series resistance is estimated within about 10 %, but 1 % soiling stays hidden in string-to-string mismatch (F1 0.25).

projects.title: Off-site canopy vs row-to-row shading in an autumn IEC 61724-1 PV acceptance test
projects.summary: A hypothetical 10 MWp single-axis tracker plant next to a real forest edge in central Poland: a 1 m Meta/WRI canopy height window read with HTTP range requests, ERA5 weather for a September 2025 PAC campaign, and synthetic SCADA from a separate plant simulator that reuses the analysis's shading geometry.
projects.highlight: Row-to-row shading under flat-terrain backtracking, not the forest, drives the shortfall (2.05 pp vs 0.18 pp; estimated 1.78 and 0.22). Excluding canopy-shaded intervals turns a failed PAC into a pass, and the raycaster matches SCADA dropouts at interval F1 0.82 but only R² 0.12.

projects.title: Kelmarsh wind farm in a laptop-GPU LES
projects.summary: A home-made D3Q19 lattice Boltzmann large-eddy simulator in ~550 lines of NVIDIA Warp kernels (regularized collision, Smagorinsky subgrid, log-law wall, actuator disks and precursor turbulence), run across all 72 wind directions on Kelmarsh and compared record-by-record with 6 years of SCADA and PyWake.
projects.highlight: With no parameter fitted to the measured losses the LES predicts 9.79 % farm wake loss against 9.24 % measured in 159,289 SCADA records (sector RMSE 2.2 pp vs 2.6 pp for PyWake Gaussian) in 81 s per wind direction on a 6 GB laptop GPU.

projects.title: A Bayesian digital twin of a wind farm
projects.summary: A probabilistic model of every Kelmarsh turbine updated day by day from SCADA: posteriors with credible intervals for efficiency, anemometer error, yaw offset, derating and bearing cooling, the probability of each fault type, lost energy by cause and inspections ranked by value of information.
projects.highlight: On 624 injected faults it names the right cause in 95 % of detections against 72 % for CUSUM and NBM charts, with 0.50 false alarms per turbine-year against 2.08.

projects.title: Wind turbine downtime, causes and availability
projects.summary: Stops, deratings and curtailment found in 10-minute SCADA without status codes (rules, power-curve residual, pitch / rotor-speed signature, HMM, gradient boosting), classified into IEC 61400-26 categories, priced in lost energy and turned into time- and energy-based availability on three open farms, with a CLI for any farm's long-format SCADA.
projects.highlight: The pitch / rotor-speed signature finds stops with F1 0.80-0.91 without training, while the usual "power ≤ 0" rule raises 4,833 alarms for 1,412 logged stops; booking grid and curtailment stops as turbine faults cuts warranty availability from 97.9 % to 93.5 %.

projects.title: Wind turbine O&M reliability from status and alarm logs
projects.summary: Turns status and alarm logs from Kelmarsh, Penmanshiel and Hill of Towie (352 turbine-years) into first-up Pareto downtime, MTBF/MTTR, Weibull and Crow-AMSAA reliability trends, bad-actor turbines, 7-day repeat bursts, alarm cascades and SCADA cross-checks.
projects.highlight: 7 of 69 codes cause 80 % of Kelmarsh stop hours; 43 % of Penmanshiel failures repeat the same code within 7 days of restart (3.5 % by chance), and Crow-AMSAA separates improving fleets (Kelmarsh beta 0.82) from deteriorating ones (Penmanshiel beta 1.12).

projects.title: WARP: wake-aware turbine verification
projects.summary: Expected power from the unwaked neighbours carried through a calibrated wake model, with CUSUM charts for power loss, derating, anemometer bias and yaw misalignment.
projects.highlight: On 288 faults injected into 2019-2020 data it finds a 3 % anemometer bias in 83 % of cases and a derating to 95 % of rated power in 94 %, where the neighbour index finds 4 %; yaw faults are found every time, partly by construction.

projects.title: Drivetrain temperatures: early fault detection
projects.summary: Normal behaviour models of nine drivetrain temperatures on Kelmarsh SCADA: a physical RC thermal model, gradient boosting and a fleet reference, validated on 8,100 injected faults, real logged events and the CARE to Compare benchmark.
projects.highlight: A +5 °C drift is caught in 97-99 % of cases within about 20 days by every method; on CARE the temperature-only models are precise but miss faults no thermometer can see.

projects.title: A fly-brain novelty detector for turbine faults
projects.summary: The fruit fly's mushroom-body novelty detector (FlyHash and the fly Bloom filter), wired with the real FlyWire projection-neuron to Kenyon-cell connectome, run as a streaming fault detector on 95 wind turbine datasets of the CARE to Compare benchmark.
projects.highlight: Honest negative result: the fly scores 0.47 against 0.51 for k-NN (0.5 is random), real wiring does no better than shuffled, and after a year of training the filter saturates and stops alarming.

projects.title: Wind power curves (IEC 61400-12-1)
projects.summary: Six years of open Kelmarsh SCADA: cleaning with event logs, power curves with IEC 61400-12-1 binning on nacelle anemometry, underperformance tracking, static yaw misalignment and lost energy.
projects.highlight: Caught a silent change of the SCADA wind speed definition that made the turbines look up to 14 % better than they were.

projects.title: Wakes and shadow flicker
projects.summary: Shadow flicker maps for the six-turbine Kelmarsh farm, as an astronomical worst case and as an expected case from sunshine, rotor operation and orientation, plus PyWake wake flow maps and annual wake losses.
projects.highlight: The worst case exceeds 30 h/year on 2.4 km² up to 860 m from the nearest turbine; sunshine, operation and rotor orientation bring the expected hours to 20 % of that.

projects.title: Untapped biogas potential in Poland
projects.summary: Manure and cereal straw from the 2020 Agricultural Census turned into methane per gmina and 15 km catchment, minus what the registered plants (KOWR) already digest, set against free DSO connection capacity and gas pipelines, with a Monte Carlo on the coefficients and a check of how well the score ranks existing plants.
projects.highlight: About 2.2 billion m³ of methane a year sits in farm residues and existing plants digest about 1.4 % of the manure; of 816 MWe within reach of published grid nodes only 473 MWe fits their free capacity.

projects.title: What is a flexible biogas plant worth?
projects.summary: Day-by-day backtest of an agricultural biogas CHP plant on Polish day-ahead prices 2024-2026: a mixed-integer plant model with engines, gas storage and a heat tank, a realizable strategy that only uses a forecast available before gate closure, a design grid of engine capacity and storage hours, support-scheme scenarios and Germany as the reference market.
projects.highlight: Twice the engine capacity and 12 h of gas storage add about 360 thousand PLN a year on a forecast alone (86 % of perfect foresight); with only 2 h of storage the extra engines earn less than a third of that.

projects.title: Which method catches a sick digester first?
projects.summary: An ADM1 (BSM2) twin of an agricultural co-digestion plant with realistic sensors and lab samples, 140 injected process upsets and instrument faults, and eight ways to catch them: FOS/TAC thresholds, EWMA and CUSUM on yield, PCA, expert rules, gradient boosting and an EKF twin, plus a check on real farm digesters.
projects.highlight: Twice-weekly FOS/TAC warns before the yield loss in 1 % of upsets; PCA on online signals does it in 75 % with 0.7 false alarms a year, and the EKF twin names all 20 CH4 analyser drifts as instrument faults without any failure examples.

projects.title: Did the upgrade work? Causal O&M verification
projects.summary: Five causal estimators (test-control bins, gradient boosting with conformal intervals, synthetic control, BSTS, difference-in-differences) validated by injecting known uplifts into real Kelmarsh wind and PVDAQ PV data, with a test-plan calculator, wake spillover and real logged events.
projects.highlight: A +3 % uplift needs about 9 weeks to prove with five control turbines, +1 % stays unproven after a year; on real events before/after reports -3.2 % to +3.0 % where the turbines came back within ±1 %.

projects.title: Fleet monitoring as code
projects.summary: Grafana dashboards, alert rules and datasource generated from Python, fed by a live replay of public wind and PV SCADA into InfluxDB 2.
projects.highlight: Alerts fire on real faults, including a PV inverter that stopped producing ten days before it reported an error code.

projects.title: Streaming SCADA ingestion, event-time watermarks and a Bronze-Silver-Gold lakehouse for wind and PV
projects.summary: A simulated 50 MW wind and PV fleet with LTE router outages, MQTT QoS-1 duplicates, Europe/Warsaw DST days and sensor faults, replayed through naive ingestion-time windows and through an event-time Bronze-Silver-Gold Parquet pipeline with upserts, counter continuity and rule-based sensor QC.
projects.highlight: Across 18 simulated LTE outages, naive windowing puts a median 9.2x the true energy into the reconnect quarter-hour (185 % nMAE in affected intervals) and loses 6.0 % of fleet energy on the 25-hour DST day. Event-time windows fix both; how much of the backlog they recover depends on the watermark: 47 % of delayed minutes at 1 h, 81 % at 2 h, 99.6 % at 4 h.

projects.title: Wind and solar outlook for Poland, live
projects.summary: A 7-day probabilistic forecast of national wind and PV generation from 122 ensemble members (ECMWF, ICON, GFS), calibrated daily against PSE data and refreshed every morning by GitHub Actions, with an ERA5 resource climatology since 1991.
projects.highlight: Day-ahead nMAE 10.5 % for solar and 17.7 % for wind over a 12-month test; the forecast beats climatology by 60-68 % in CRPS.

projects.title: A citable forecast benchmark for the Polish grid
projects.summary: Wind, solar, demand and day-ahead price forecasts for Poland at 15-minute resolution, day-ahead (issued at 10:00 on D-1) and intraday, with fixed data, splits and metrics and a strict as-of rule enforced by leakage tests; eleven reference models from persistence and the PSE plan to gradient boosting and zero-shot Chronos, TimesFM and Toto foundation models, with a public leaderboard, a monthly live track and a Zenodo DOI.
projects.highlight: Intraday models beat the PSE plan by 20-26 %; day-ahead nothing that respects the 10:00 issue time beats it for volumes, and the price is the one task a foundation model wins (Chronos-2 with weather covariates, 88.5 PLN/MWh MAE, 9 % better than gradient boosting).

projects.title: Build Poland's power mix with sliders
projects.summary: An hourly merit-order toy that runs entirely in the browser: set PV, onshore and offshore wind, storage, nuclear, gas, coal and interconnectors, pick a weather year 2010-2025, and see curtailment, energy not served, CO2 and an approximate price; every scenario is a shareable link.
projects.highlight: Coal out by 2030 without new firm capacity leaves 6-10 TWh unserved in every weather year; the 2040 plan makes curtailment the main issue (17-24 % of wind and PV).

projects.title: Capacity credit of wind and PV in Poland
projects.summary: Multi-state Markov models of wind and PV from ERA5 at 29 points, sequential Monte Carlo LOLE/EENS on IEEE RTS-79 and real PSE demand, and an ELCC map of Poland: the method of the author's MSc thesis rebuilt on open data, extended with battery ELCC and multi-day lulls from a regime-switching weather model.
projects.highlight: Reproduces the IEEE RTS-79 reference LOLE exactly; wind ELCC about 26.5 % and PV about 10 %, compared with capacity market derating factors.

projects.title: Ramps and flexibility needs of the Polish grid
projects.summary: Residual load from PSE data since 2020: ramp distributions, the evening ramp after sunset, midday minima, the IRRE flexibility metric and battery needs with +20 % and +50 % PV.
projects.highlight: The evening ramp grew from 1.5 to 4.3 GW between 2021 and 2025; the P99 hourly ramp is 3.2 GW, against 4.6 GW PSE expects for 2030.

projects.title: PV and wind curtailed by the Polish TSO
projects.summary: Non-market redispatch of PV and wind by PSE from the reports API and parsed system announcements since late 2023: volumes, drivers, overlap with negative prices and the value of curtailed energy under the published compensation formula.
projects.highlight: 1.8 TWh curtailed in 2026 to 25 Oct, 50 % more than a year earlier; 98 % for balancing reasons and most of it at positive prices.

projects.title: How good is ERA5 in Poland?
projects.summary: ERA5 and CERRA reanalyses checked against 19 IMGW-PIB synoptic stations and Kelmarsh hub-height wind: bias by season and hour, the error in energy, and long-term (MCP) correction.
projects.highlight: ERA5 overstates 10 m wind by 8 % (median), about 15 % in wind energy; the matrix MCP method cuts the energy error from 41 % to 5 %.

projects.title: Can a fly brain forecast wind and solar?
projects.summary: The FlyWire connectome of the fruit fly brain used as an echo state network reservoir to forecast Polish wind and PV generation, against random and rewired reservoirs, ridge, gradient boosting and the PSE day-ahead plan.
projects.highlight: No: tuned separately, the fly brain matches a random reservoir within 2 %; its compressed eigenvalue spectrum makes it robust to bad settings, not a better forecaster.

projects.title: Grid connection studies and non-firm capacity on Polish MV/110 kV feeders
projects.summary: Steady-state and N-1 study of a synthetic Polish 110/15 kV GPZ and four radial 15 kV feeders built from catalogue conductor data, solved with a polar Newton-Raphson Ybus power flow: hosting capacity under unity power factor, cos-phi(P) and Q(U), annual reactive energy, export caps with a battery, and cable pooling under N-1.
projects.highlight: On a 14.2 km overhead feeder cos-phi(P) and Q(U) lift hosting capacity from 2.30 MW to 3.21 and 3.11 MW, but cost capacity on a thermally limited cable feeder; on a PVGIS profile a 70 % export cap curtails 6.53 % of PV energy, and pooling wind behind the same 21.54 MW connection carries 1.99 times the energy of firm PV.

projects.title: res-asset-kpi: KPI library for PV, wind and BESS
projects.summary: An open-source Python library on PyPI, with a Zenodo DOI, for the indicators asset managers report every month: PR and weather-corrected PR, contract availability for PV, wind (IEC 61400-26 categories) and batteries, the budget-to-actual energy bridge, power curves and AEP, MTBF/MTTR and Crow-AMSAA, SoC-corrected round-trip efficiency, cycles, capacity tests with uncertainty and contract damages set in YAML.
projects.highlight: Extracted from six analysis projects and reproducing their results exactly (41 checks over about a million values, largest relative difference 1.3e-13); a hand-worked test for every formula, Hypothesis property tests, mypy strict, CI on Python 3.11-3.13.

projects.title: pse-opendata: Python client for PSE data
projects.summary: An open-source library for the public data of the Polish TSO: 16 reports plus the legacy CSV export since 2009 as tidy pandas frames with explicit interval times in UTC and local time, monthly Parquet cache aware of PSE's late corrections, and a CLI.
projects.highlight: Offline tests on recorded responses plus live checks against PSE's API description; documents pitfalls such as DST labels, the 100,000-row cap and pagination that drops rows.
